open_questions: Which take of Bags' Groove the Songsterr tab follows is not named; both takes measure 146.
Swing to Bop's pianist is disputed (Kenny Kersey or Thelonious Monk); the drummer is not.
His triplet runs on Love Me or Leave Me (290) and Two Not One (238) are past the sextuplet ceiling of 190 and are approximated as swung eighths.
Equipment is not sourced: no brand or sizes for his kit are given here.
The MJQ (Django), Walkin' and Ascenseur pour l'echafaud tracks have no human transcription and are not scored.
Bishop's 1941 Hot House intro was not used: a commenter credits Sid Catlett, and Bishop could not settle it.

identity.name: Kenny Clarke

evidence.note: A heart attack at his home; he and his wife had settled in Montreuil.

identity.summary: The house drummer at Minton's whose ride-cymbal time and bass-drum "bombs" became bebop drumming.

alter_egos.name: Klook
alter_egos.context: Short for 'Klook-mop', in imitation of a rimshot followed directly by a bass-drum bomb.

alter_egos.name: Liaquat Ali Salaam
alter_egos.context: The name he took on converting to Islam in 1946.

traditions.impact: Played snare in the band of the Coleman Industrial Home in Pittsburgh at eight or nine.

eras.label: Teddy Hill and Minton's
eras.context: From Edgar Hayes and Teddy Hill's band (where he moved the time to the ride cymbal) to house drummer at Minton's Playhouse, where bebop was worked out in the after-hours jams.
defining_traits: the time on the ride cymbal

eras.label: Gillespie, the MJQ and Prestige
eras.context: Gillespie's big band and sextet; Paris 1948-51; the Modern Jazz Quartet 1951-55; Miles Davis's Prestige sessions of 1954; house drummer at Savoy and at Van Gelder's ('Klook's corner').
defining_traits: light, quiet cymbal and bass drum
ruffs, triplets and short rolls on a tight snare

eras.label: Paris and the Clarke-Boland Big Band
eras.context: Paris from 1956: the Blue Note and the Club Saint-Germain, Ascenseur pour l'echafaud with Miles Davis, the Three Bosses with Bud Powell, the Kenny Clarke/Francy Boland Big Band 1961-72; a drum school with Dante Agostini.
defining_traits: softer than most drummers in a big band

evidence.note: 'Clarke follows feelings, lives inside the pulse' (Korall, quoted).

swing.notes: 'A strong quarter note groove' on Swing to Bop; the eighths swung, flattening with the tempo (Bishop's fours at 238 and 290).

dynamics.balance: 'His cymbal sound and bass drum work were light and quietly persuasive'; in the big band 'Playing softer than most drummers' (Korall, quoted on Wikipedia).

feel_profile.interaction: Comping with the snare on the 'and' of 1 or of 3 (the Kenny note), and from the 1930s playing the brass and saxophone figures with the band: 'play the figures over the regular beat'.

hand_techniques.name: Brushes
hand_techniques.description: The swing rhythm on the snare with the left hand in the gap (Swing to Bop); fours on brushes at 290, ties for sweeps (Love Me or Leave Me).

hand_techniques.name: Rudiments on the snare
hand_techniques.description: 'well-executed ruffs, triplets, short rolls on a tightly tuned snare' (Korall); paradiddle triplet licks, five-stroke rolls, four-stroke ruffs and stick shots in his fours (Two Not One).

coordination.notes: The time moved to the ride cymbal to free the left hand; exercises for independence of the bass drum and snare under the ride, written with Gillespie (Wikipedia).

searched: Todd Bishop's transcriptions, read bar by bar: Swing to Bop (91 bars), Love Me or Leave Me (eight fours), Two Not One (eight fours), The Kenny Note (Apothegm's head)
The Songsterr tab of Bags' Groove (242 bars)
devices_search.note: No device written: quarter-note triplets in one four of Love Me or Leave Me and half-note triplets in one of Two Not One are rhythms within the bar, not a cross-rhythm, grouping or metric device kept across bar lines.

foot_techniques.name: Bombs
foot_techniques.description: The bass drum for irregular accents ('dropping bombs') instead of four on the floor; the hi-hat on the backbeats.

foot_techniques.name: Feathered bass drum
foot_techniques.description: 'You can assume that he's feathering the bass drum throughout' (Bishop, Swing to Bop).

sound_profile.cymbal_character: 'His cymbal sound and bass drum work were light and quietly persuasive' (Korall).

sample_hints.50s: A small jazz kit, a light ride, a tight snare, a soft bass drum.

signature_traits.label: The time on the ride cymbal
signature_traits.description: He came upon the ride cymbal for the time on a fast tune with Teddy Hill, freeing the left hand.

signature_traits.label: Dropping bombs
signature_traits.description: Irregular accents on the bass drum; a rimshot followed directly by a bomb gave him his name, Klook.

signature_traits.label: The Kenny note
signature_traits.description: Comping with the snare on the 'and' of 1 or of 3 (Apothegm).

signature_traits.label: The cross-stick on 4
signature_traits.description: Under the solos of Bags' Groove, 190 of the tab's 242 bars.

patterns.name: Apothegm: the Kenny note
patterns.function: The ride and the foot on 2 and 4, the snare on the 'and' of 3.

evidence.note: Bishop's two-measure phrase, its second bar.

patterns.name: Bags' Groove: the cross-stick on 4
patterns.function: The ride swung, the foot on 2 and 4, the cross-stick on 4.

patterns.name: Swing to Bop: the time on brushes
patterns.function: The ride rhythm on the snare with brushes, the left hand in the gap.

evidence.note: Bishop bars 2, 4-6, 8, 10; the foot is a reconstruction.

affiliations.name: Miles Davis
affiliations.notes: The Prestige sessions of 1954 (Walkin', Bags' Groove) and Ascenseur pour l'echafaud in Paris.

evidence.note: At the 1939 World's Fair Webb 'strongly influenced him and encouraged his rhythmic explorations'.
Gillespie encouraged the ride-cymbal time; they wrote independence exercises together.

philosophy.idea: Play along with the brass and saxophone figures, to emphasise and support their lines: the drummer outlines the band, not only the time.

innovations: The time kept on the ride cymbal rather than the hi-hat
The bass drum for irregular accents, 'dropping bombs'
The hi-hat foot on 2 and 4 under the ride: the bebop drum kit's division of labour

cultural_references.description: 'Oop bop sh'bam a klook a mop': his nickname in the lyric of Gillespie's Oop Bop Sh'Bam.

common_misconceptions: That bebop drumming began with Max Roach: Clarke's ride-cymbal time came first, with Teddy Hill and at Minton's; Roach became the leading bebop drummer while Clarke was in the army (Wikipedia).

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A small 1950s jazz kit, a light ride, a tight snare, a soft feathered bass drum
generation_rules: The time on the ride, the foot on 2 and 4, the bass drum feathered.
The snare on the 'and' of 1 or of 3; bombs dropped on the bass drum, not kept.
avoid: Four on the floor played loud

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: From Chick Webb and the swing bands to the ride-cymbal time of bebop; Max Roach, Art Blakey, Roy Haynes and Philly Joe Jones built on it.
